canonical_definition: Commonsense Reasoning refers to the ability to reason about everyday physical and social situations using general world knowledge, often operationalized via benchmarks like HellaSwag, PIQA, Winogrande, or ARC that assess plausibility judgments, multi-hop inference, or zero-shot task performance. While some definitions emphasize selecting contextually appropriate continuations or answers requiring implicit reasoning strategies, others extend to multimodal contexts (e.g., visual commonsense for scene interpretation) or structured reasoning over explanation graphs, reflecting variations in scope but shared focus on grounding in everyday knowledge.
